Testimony.subtitle: Discover feedback from companies that chose Jupiter Safe to strengthen their QHSE performance and regulatory compliance.

id1.review: We are very satisfied with the result delivered by NextÉclat. The branding and website perfectly reflect our business and professional image. The team understood our needs and created a modern, clear digital presence suited to our clients.

id2.review: We are very satisfied with the design and development of our Falcon Beats platform. NextÉclat created a professional visual identity and a user experience tailored to selling our beats. Since its launch, the platform lets us showcase and sell our creations efficiently.

id3.review: We are very satisfied with the website designed by NextÉclat. The project highlighted our expertise, services, and QHSE solutions for our clients. The team perfectly translated our vision with a professional design and a clear presentation of our activities.

id4.review: We are very satisfied with the final result of the video produced by NextÉclat. The production quality, the team's professionalism, and their respect of deadlines far exceeded our expectations. Every detail was carefully executed to create content that matched our vision.

id5.review: We are very happy with the video produced by NextÉclat. The concept we imagined was perfectly translated on screen, and the result matches our expectations exactly. A big thank you to the team for their professionalism, creativity, and commitment throughout the project.

id6.review: We are very satisfied with the final result of the video produced by NextÉclat. Taking advantage of our stay in the Netherlands during the holidays to complete this project on a tight schedule was a great opportunity. The team showed great professionalism to achieve the desired result.

id7.review: We are very satisfied with the video produced by NextÉclat. The quality of the final result, the creativity, and the team's professionalism brought our vision to life. The project was carried out with care and every detail was worked on thoroughly.

EducationTraining.Subtitle1: The Hague University of Applied Sciences — Netherlands
EducationTraining.Paragraphe1: This program gave me a multidisciplinary foundation in communication, design, UX/UI, digital design and multimedia content creation. Projects could take many different forms: websites, mobile applications, intranets, infographics, digital experiences, videos or multimedia concepts. This program laid the foundations of my current profile, at the intersection of design, communication and digital project development.
EducationTraining.Paragraphe2: This training allowed me to go beyond design and turn a visual concept into a fully functional web application. I developed my skills in HTML, CSS, JavaScript, React and responsive design, as well as Git, GitHub, API integration and deployment. I then put these skills into practice by developing my own portfolio and several web projects for clients.
EducationTraining.Paragraphe3: This certificate allowed me to acquire the fundamentals of electronic music production: beatmaking, composition, arrangement, sound design, MIDI, sampling, recording, as well as the basics of mixing and mastering.
EducationTraining.Paragraphe4: A significant part of my skills comes not only from my academic training, but also from regular hands-on practice through various projects: music videos, advertising spots, productions for artists, weddings, workshops and continuous self-learning.

OurWebDesignProjects.subtitle: Web projects that bring ideas to life
OurWebDesignProjects.contentTitle: Discover 3 of our recent projects, each carefully designed to meet specific needs. More projects are currently under development. Whether it’s a showcase website, a website for artists or influencers, an online store, or a custom digital solution, we create without limits.

project.contentLine1: NextÉclat is a digital agency that supports entrepreneurs, artists, and influencers in building a strong brand image. We designed this website to showcase our expertise in branding, web design, audiovisual production, and digital content creation.
project.contentLine2: Falcon Beats is a music platform we created for artists and creators looking for high-quality professional beats. It allows users to explore, purchase, and download various instrumentals adapted to different music styles, accessible worldwide.
project.contentLine3: I designed the website for Cyrus FP, a company specializing in the installation of flags in various sizes. The website highlights their expertise in installing large-scale flags and their visual communication solutions.
project.contentLine4: We designed the showcase website for Pasha Bouw, a company specialized in renovation and custom projects. The website highlights its expertise in home renovations, bathrooms, and kitchens, as well as its commitment to quality and tailored solutions for each client.
project.contentLine5: We designed the showcase website for Jupiter Safe Consulting, a company specialized in QHSE consulting. The website highlights its expertise in compliance, risk prevention, and continuous improvement, with solutions adapted to businesses’ needs.
project.contentLine6: Personal portfolio designed to showcase my skills in UX Design, Front-End Development, visual identity creation, and branding, with expertise in audiovisual production. Through this selection, I offer an overview of my journey, my creative approach, and the various projects I have developed over the years.

Intro.Title: Phases & Design Methodology
Intro.Subtitle: From the initial idea to launch, every project follows a structured framework: the six phases of the P6 method, Jesse James Garrett's UX approach, and the research methods and techniques that ensure the quality of every design decision.

Section1.Title: A Structured Approach with the P6 Method
Section1.Intro1: When developing the concepts for my applications, I use Roel Grit's P6 method to structure each project in a clear and methodical way. This approach gives me an overall view of the project, lets me define the different stages of execution, and lets me track their progress, from design through to implementation.
Section1.Intro2: Each phase acts as a frame of reference that helps me stay on track throughout development. The P6 method allows me to turn an idea into a concrete project, moving forward step by step while keeping a coherent view of the objectives, needs and expected results.

Phase1.Title: Initiative Phase
Phase1.Text: During the initiative phase, a problem or idea is identified and it is decided that action should be taken. The following activities take place during this phase:
Phase1.List3: Determination of the project's objective and expected outcome

Phase2.Title: Definition Phase
Phase2.Text: The definition phase makes it possible to clearly determine what is expected from the project. By the end of this phase, an action plan is drawn up in which the project is precisely defined.

Phase3.Title: Design Phase
Phase3.Text: During the design phase, the appearance and functioning of the solution are determined. To check whether the envisioned solution meets the defined requirements, a prototype can be created if necessary.

Phase4.Title: Preparation Phase
Phase4.Text: During the preparation phase, the product resulting from the design phase is prepared for its implementation. The product is not yet developed at this stage; the goal is to put in place all the conditions needed for a smooth execution.

Phase5.Title: Execution Phase
Phase5.Text: This is the phase where the actual development work begins. The final product is built in line with the plans and specifications defined in the previous phases.

Phase6.Title: Follow-up Phase (Post-execution)
Phase6.Text: During this phase, the result of the project is put into use. As circumstances and needs may evolve over time, the requirements related to the product may also change. Adjustments and improvements may then become necessary.

Section2.Title: User Experience Design
Section2.Intro1: For the development of my applications, I use Jesse James Garrett's User Experience design method. It allows me to design user-centered applications that take into account users' needs, expectations and goals.
Section2.Intro2: This approach guides me from defining requirements through to designing the final interface. It allows me to structure every step of the UX process and create intuitive, accessible and consistent experiences. The method is built on five complementary planes — Strategy, Scope, Structure, Skeleton and Surface — which let me move progressively from strategic thinking to the visual design of the application.

Plane1.Text: User needs and expectations are identified through user-needs research and target-audience analysis. The goal is to adapt the application to users' needs and expectations. The application's objectives are also defined to clearly determine what the user should be able to achieve with the application.

Plane2.Text: System requirements are defined to clearly determine the features and content specifications the application must include.

Plane3.Text: This plane determines how the different system requirements and application features relate to one another and how they are organized.

Plane4.Text: This plane determines how the user navigates within the application. The site's wireframes are also designed to define the structure and layout of the different interface elements.

Plane5.Text: The application's visual design is created to define its final appearance. This step covers the colour palette, icons, typography, brand visual identity and the overall look & feel of the application.

Section3.Title: My Working Methods
Section3.Intro: To guarantee the quality and consistency of my project results, I rely on several methods that structure every stage of my working process.

Method1.Title: Project management — Roel Grit's P6 method
Method1.Text: I use the P6 method to structure my projects, define the different stages and ensure clear tracking from the initial idea through to completion.

Method2.Title: Research methodology — Nel Verhoeven
Method2.Text: For my research and analysis, I rely on Nel Verhoeven's methodology to carry out my research in a structured and methodical way.

Method3.Title: User Experience Design — Jesse James Garrett
Method3.Text: For the development of my applications, I use Jesse James Garrett's User Experience method. It allows me to design solutions that are centred on the user and adapted to the needs of a specific target audience.

Section4.Title: Research & Evaluation Techniques
Section4.Intro: These techniques structure my research and testing phases, from identifying user needs through to validating the prototype.

Technique1.Title: Expert Review
Technique1.Text: To identify usability issues on the existing site before its redesign, an expert review is carried out. This analysis helps identify the main areas for improvement, using Jakob Nielsen's usability heuristics as a reference framework (Nielsen, 1995).

Technique2.Title: Semi-structured Interview
Technique2.Text: To identify users' needs and expectations, a semi-structured interview is conducted. This method offers a degree of freedom in gathering information and allows open-ended questions to be asked, while also exploring certain topics further through follow-up questions. It provides more precise and detailed information about the target audience's expectations.

Technique3.Title: Target Audience Study
Technique3.Text: To better understand the website's users, a target audience study is carried out. An interview with the client first helps identify the known characteristics of users. The target audience is then consulted to complete this information and identify needs and characteristics that are not yet known.

Technique4.Title: Benchmarking
Technique4.Text: To identify relevant features, navigation patterns and visual choices for the prototype, a comparative analysis (benchmark) is carried out. Analysing similar websites helps identify their strengths for inspiration, as well as their weaknesses to learn from during design. This approach also helps pinpoint concrete ways to improve the site's user experience and usability.

Technique5.Title: MoSCoW Method
Technique5.Text: To prioritise the prototype's functional and technical requirements, the MoSCoW method is used. It allows features to be ranked by importance and identifies those that are essential, desirable, or can be postponed. This approach keeps the project feasible, coherent and manageable.

Technique6.Title: Use Cases and Scenarios
Technique6.Text: To anticipate the different situations that may arise while using the site, use cases and scenarios are developed. These tools help analyse the application from the user's point of view and simulate the most common situations to prepare the various prototype testing stages.

Technique7.Title: Usability Test
Technique7.Text: To check whether the prototype meets usability requirements, a test is carried out with the target audience. This test makes it possible to observe and analyse how users navigate the site and carry out the tasks assigned to them. Observations are recorded in an observation sheet and an evaluation grid to facilitate analysis. An interview is also conducted with participants to gather their impressions, comments and suggestions about the prototype.

Technique8.Title: Survey
Technique8.Text: To gather information from a larger number of people, a survey is conducted among the target audience. This method makes it possible to collect structured data on users' needs, expectations, habits and preferences. The survey can be carried out using a questionnaire with both closed and open questions. The results help guide design choices and develop a solution better suited to the target audience.

Technique9.Title: Desk Research
Technique9.Text: Desk research is also carried out to gather and analyse information already available on the project's subject. This research draws on scientific articles, studies, reports, books, specialised websites and other reliable sources. Desk research also makes it possible to compare different sources, verify certain information and identify trends or best practices relevant to the project.

Principles.Title: Research and Evaluation Principles
Principles.Subtitle: To guarantee the reliability and quality of the information used throughout the project, the following principles are applied.

Principle1.Title: Source Reliability
Principle1.Text: The sources used for research come from reliable and relevant references to guarantee the quality of the information gathered.

Principle2.Title: Source Currency
Principle2.Text: Where possible, the articles, studies and other sources consulted are recent and less than ten years old, to ensure the information used is up to date.

Principle3.Title: Source Referencing
Principle3.Text: The various sources consulted throughout the project are referenced according to APA standards, to ensure clear traceability of the information used.

Principle4.Title: Usability Evaluation
Principle4.Text: To assess whether the interfaces designed meet usability principles, I rely in particular on Jakob Nielsen's usability heuristics (Nielsen, 1995). These principles serve as a reference for identifying potential usability issues and improving the user experience.

Banner.title: Fitness Friends - Mobile Application
Banner.Content: Fitness Friends is a mobile application designed to help fitness enthusiasts meet workout partners and participate in group training sessions at the gym of their choice.

Description.title: Description
Description.paragraphe1: is a mobile application that I envisioned and designed to make it easier for fitness enthusiasts to meet people they can train with. The idea is simple: find a workout partner who shares the same goals, join a group workout session, or simply meet new people at your gym.
Description.paragraphe2: The application makes workouts more social and motivating by creating a connection between people who want to progress together. Everyone can choose their gym, discover nearby partners, and participate in workout sessions that match their preferences.
Description.paragraphe3: Through this project, I worked on the concept, user experience, interface, and visual identity of the application, with the goal of creating an experience that is simple, modern, and enjoyable to use.

Conception.title: Design
Conception.Subtitle: How the application works
Conception.paragraphe1: With FitnessFriend, fitness enthusiasts can create their own profile by adding personal information and photos to introduce themselves to potential workout partners. They can also specify their preferences, goals, and the type of partner they would like to train with.
Conception.paragraphe2: Once their profile has been created, users can discover other fitness enthusiasts on the platform and connect with people who share similar interests and fitness goals. They can send messages, respond to requests, and communicate with each other to find a workout partner who suits them.
Conception.paragraphe3: FitnessFriend also allows users to view the social media profiles of a potential partner, such as Instagram, Facebook, or TikTok, in order to get to know each other better and build a relationship that goes beyond the application.
Conception.paragraphe4: Users can also share meal plans, exchange advice, and support each other in achieving their goals. The goal of FitnessFriend is to create a real fitness community where everyone can stay motivated, work out together, and make progress together.

ActionPlan.Title: Action Plan
ActionPlan.Content: After defining the project, I developed an implementation plan to have a clear overview of the process and the steps required to achieve my objective. This action plan includes:
ActionPlan.Line1: An overview of the activities, phases, and deliverables to be produced throughout the project, as well as the methods and techniques used,
ActionPlan.Line2: The requirements that ensure the quality of the final result as well as the intermediate deliverables,
ActionPlan.Line3: An overview of all stakeholders and organizations that have an influence on the project, including the role of each team member,
ActionPlan.Line4: A project schedule with the different deadlines,
ActionPlan.Line5: A description of the project's duration, scope, and prerequisites,
ActionPlan.Line6: The cost of the project as well as all risk factors.

UsedMethod.Title: Methods Used
UsedMethod.Content1: To structure the entire project, I used the P6 project management method developed by Dutch project management expert Roel Grit. I chose this method because it makes it possible to approach a project as a whole: each phase contains specific activities, providing a clear framework throughout the project. The P6 method consists of six phases.
UsedMethod.Content2: For the design of this mobile application, I used the User Experience method created by American designer Jesse James Garrett. I chose this method because it allowed me to develop an application tailored to a specific target audience, making the app accessible and relevant. During the project, I applied this method during the design phase of P6.
UsedMethod.Content3: I chose to conduct the different research activities for the project according to the method of Dutch researcher Nel Verhoeven, a recognized and respected research consultant in the Netherlands.

UsedTechnic.Title: Techniques Used
UsedTechnic.Content1: This technique makes it possible to determine the needs and expectations of users. It provides greater freedom when collecting information by asking open-ended questions that generate detailed answers and a substantial amount of information about the target audience.
UsedTechnic.Content2: This technique allowed me to identify the possible characteristics of the actual users of the application, helping me better determine which profiles to approach during the interview sessions.
UsedTechnic.Content3: This technique allowed me to determine the application's features, navigation, and overall visual direction by drawing inspiration from applications comparable to my concept. This study also allowed me to identify the weaknesses of these applications in order to better position my own application in the market.
UsedTechnic.Content4: I also used the MoSCoW method, which allows application requirements to be prioritized by grouping them according to their level of importance, helping to better understand the essential needs of the project.
UsedTechnic.Content5: A use case makes it possible to visualize all the alternative scenarios that may occur when a user is trying to achieve their goal. It also establishes the basis for the functional and non-functional requirements.
UsedTechnic.Content6: This technique allowed me to evaluate whether the prototype met usability criteria. It makes it possible to test and evaluate user behavior while navigating through the application by observing how the user moves through the different steps of the user journey.

SystemRequirements.Title: Application Requirements
SystemRequirements.Paragraph1: At this stage of my project, I defined the needs and requirements of the FitnessFriend application in order to clearly determine the features and characteristics it needed to meet.
SystemRequirements.Paragraph2: For this, I relied on the results of my research phase, including the benchmark, user needs, and the objectives of the application.
SystemRequirements.Paragraph3: I then classified these requirements into two categories: functional and non-functional. Functional requirements describe the features that the user must be able to use, while non-functional requirements concern how the application should operate, particularly in terms of performance, security, simplicity, and reliability.
SystemRequirements.Paragraph4: This distinction allowed me to structure the project's needs more clearly and better define the foundations of FitnessFriend.

VisualDeisgn.Title: Visual Design
VisualDeisgn.Paragraph1: At this stage, I created the visual design of the website as it will appear in its final version. I designed the necessary elements to transform the website into its final visual design. For this, I:
VisualDeisgn.Line7: Designed the mockups for the different pages of the application
VisualDeisgn.Paragraph2: When creating the visual design, I relied on the results of the user research, benchmark study, and application objectives to ensure that the design was perfectly aligned with them.

ColorScheme.Title: Color Palette
ColorScheme.Paragraph: To differentiate the FitnessFriend brand from its competitors, I selected a new color palette and created a unique visual identity.

Logo.Title: FitnessFriend Logo
Logo.Content: I also created a logo to give the FitnessFriend application a brand identity. You can discover this logo in the image alongside.

Typography.Title: Typography
Typography.Content: For the FitnessFriend application, I used the Helvetica typeface, a highly readable font that is internationally recognized for its versatility. I used this typeface in different colors and sizes to create contrast between headings and body text. In certain parts of the application, I used lighter colors for secondary text to make it less prominent and allow the most important text to stand out more clearly to the user.

Icons.Title: Icons
Icons.ContentLine1: For the FitnessFriend application, I chose to use the icons
Icons.ContentLine2: These are very popular icons that are easily recognizable by users. Another advantage of Font Awesome icons is that some of them are available for free.

Wireframes.Title: Wireframes
Wireframes.Content: For the FitnessFriend application, I created wireframes to visualize the layout of the website. These wireframes provided me with a reference framework during the design of the mockups in the next stage.

Mockups.Title: Mockups
Mockups.Content: After creating the website wireframes, I designed the FitnessFriend mockups. For this, I used Figma, a platform for designing digital products such as interactive prototypes and websites. When designing the mockups, I relied on the wireframes created in the previous stage in order to continue the design logic established earlier. I also took the color palette from my style guide into account so that I could easily apply colors to the different parts of the website. During this process, I also relied on the typography defined earlier.

Result.Title: Results
Result.Content: Explore the 28 screens of the FitnessFriend app. Use the navigation buttons or swipe to browse through all the screens and gradually discover the experience offered by the application.

Banner.Title: From My Studies to Today
Banner.Content: I’m Michael Ilunga, a Front-End Developer, UX Designer, and visual identity designer, with expertise in audiovisual production. Through this portfolio, discover my expertise and a selection of projects I’ve created over the years.

WhoAreWe.Title: Who am I?
WhoAreWe.Subtitle2: is a Front-End Developer, UX Designer and creative professional passionate about creating modern, functional and visually impactful digital experiences.
WhoAreWe.ContentLine1b: Creating modern, responsive and high-performing websites using Front-end technologies.
WhoAreWe.ContentLine2b: Designing intuitive interfaces and experiences focused on users' needs.
WhoAreWe.ContentLine3b: Creating consistent visual identities through design, logos and various communication materials.
WhoAreWe.ContentLine4b: Creating visual content, photography and audiovisual productions to bring ideas and projects to life.
WhoAreWe.ContentLine5b: A multidisciplinary approach combining technology, design and creativity to create unique digital experiences.

FounderMichael.Paragraphe1: I was born in Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of the Congo, where I completed my primary and secondary education at Collège Boboto. I also grew up in a multicultural and multilingual environment, where I learned French, the official language of the country, as well as Lingala and Swahili. This cultural diversity naturally influenced the way I communicate, create and see the world.
FounderMichael.Paragraphe2: I later moved to the Netherlands, where I continued my academic and professional journey. I started by studying Marketing and Communication at ROC Zeeland in Middelburg. I then continued my studies at The Hague University of Applied Sciences in The Hague, where I earned a Bachelor of Science in Communication & Multimedia Design. These programs allowed me to develop my skills in communication, marketing, digital design, UX/UI, multimedia and creative problem-solving.
FounderMichael.Paragraphe3: Driven by my passion for technology and digital experiences, I later completed a Front-End Developer program at Novi University in Utrecht. There, I strengthened my skills in HTML, CSS, JavaScript and React, learning how to transform concepts and designs into modern, responsive and functional web experiences. My journey in the digital world has therefore gradually developed at the intersection of design, user experience and web development.
FounderMichael.Paragraphe4: My creative journey has also developed in the fields of audiovisual production and music. I studied electronic music production at SAE Institute in Rotterdam, where I learned sound creation, recording and professional music production for platforms such as Spotify and Deezer. I also gained experience in art direction through the production of music videos, advertising spots and visual projects for various brands.
FounderMichael.Paragraphe5: My international journey has also enriched my language skills. After moving to the Netherlands, I learned Dutch and significantly improved my English, which I had previously only studied at a basic level. My various music-related activities in Belgium and France also allowed me to further strengthen my French. Today, this linguistic and cultural diversity is an integral part of my identity and the way I work.
FounderMichael.Paragraphe6: Today, I bring all these experiences together to build a multidisciplinary profile at the intersection of Front-End Development, UX/UI, design, audiovisual production and creativity. My goal is to create modern, useful and visually impactful digital experiences while bringing both a technical and creative perspective to every project.

I want to contribute fully to achieving the goals of the team and the company, share my knowledge, and bring my creativity and expertise. I also want to continue learning: working alongside experienced professionals is an opportunity for me to discover new methods, develop new skills, and grow by learning from different areas of expertise.
MissionVision.Content2: In the long term, my ambition is to continue developing in the field of IT and become a more well-rounded professional. After strengthening my expertise in Front-End Development, I want to deepen my knowledge of Back-End Development and then progressively explore areas such as cybersecurity and artificial intelligence. My goal is to gradually build a versatile profile, capable of understanding and contributing to different stages of designing and developing digital solutions.
